erp.h1: ERP for NDT and Inspection Companies — Certifications, Calibration, Dispatch and Reports in One System
erp.intro: Atlantis ERP is NDT ERP software that runs an inspection company on one system: technician certifications, equipment calibration, crew dispatch, method-specific NDT reports, quotes and invoicing, with every other business app you need alongside. It is set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, an ASNT Level III-led company, so it is configured around how inspection work is controlled and audited. Fully customizable, and shown running on your own workflow before you commit.
erp.ctaNote: A guided walkthrough or a 14-day free trial is available. Trial access and setup are agreed before you start.

deliver.heading: What you get with Atlantis ERP
deliver.intro: The points a buyer should be able to check before choosing any inspection ERP, and how Atlantis answers each one.

items.h: Modules: connected apps on one database
items.p: One database runs the whole job: CRM and quotations, projects and crew dispatch, NDT reports, certificates, procedures, equipment and calibration, timesheets and expenses, purchasing and inventory, employees, payroll and time off, eLearning and dashboards. Every app is configured for NDT work, so a technician's certificate, an instrument's calibration and a job's timesheet are never typed in twice.

items.h: Reporting: method-specific NDT reports, signed and sent
items.p: Technicians fill in UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, PAUT, TOFD and other method reports in an offline field app, add photos and sign on screen. Each report moves from draft to review, approval and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures on your own versioned templates, and clients see their reports in the client portal. Approved reports can also be placed on a 3D model of the asset with Digital Twin Reporting.

items.h: Certification tracking: nobody goes to site out of date
items.p: Certification management starts with one register: every technician certificate is recorded by scheme, level and method, and its status is worked out automatically: active, expiring soon or expired. Certificate and vision-test expiries raise warning tasks well before they lapse, timesheets warn when a certificate is not valid, and planners cannot double-book a technician or an instrument serial number. Instruments are tracked by serial number with calibration records, due dates and expiry alerts, and planners are warned when assigned equipment is out of calibration.

items.h: Deployment: your hosting, your data, a phased rollout
items.p: It runs as a cloud service, or on your own infrastructure where data-residency rules require it, and the hosting location is agreed before go-live. Rollout starts where the pain is sharpest, usually certifications, calibration or reporting, and your certification records, equipment registry and client list are migrated as part of onboarding. Access rights, backups and retention are written into the rollout plan, your records stay exportable, and an open REST API supports connections to external systems, scoped and tested for your implementation.

items.h: Support: set up by people who run inspection programmes
items.p: Atlantis NDT configures, implements and supports the system itself, with dedicated implementation, staff training through the eLearning app, workflow customization and custom apps built on request. Because the company is led by an ASNT NDT Level III, procedures, certifications and report approvals are set up the way an auditor will read them.

faq.q: What does an NDT consulting engagement deliver?
faq.a: Signed documents your auditors can follow: a written practice, procedures and technique sheets, examination records and certification files, or an audit gap list with responses. The proposal names the deliverables, the methods covered and who signs each document.

faq.q: Can an outside Level III certify our technicians?
faq.a: No. Under SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 the employer certifies its own people. An outside Level III authors and approves the technical documents, prepares and grades examinations, and signs in the capacity your written practice assigns to the Level III.

faq.q: Which certification schemes do you work to?
faq.a: Employer written practices to ASNT SNT-TC-1A and ANSI/ASNT CP-189. ISO 9712 and PCN certification is examined by their own accredited bodies.

faq.q: What is the method scope constraint?
faq.a: A Level III may approve procedures and qualify personnel only in the methods they hold. Every proposal therefore names the methods it covers; founder-led work covers UT, RT, MT, PT and VT.

faq.q: Is the work remote or on site?
faq.a: Document work, reviews and most audits are delivered remotely. Witnessing, practical examinations or a site walk-through are scheduled on site when the work needs them, and scoped separately so desk work is not charged at site rates.
Each engagement is quoted on request as a defined scope, after a scoping call, because the work depends on your methods, number of technicians, codes and deadline.

faq.q: What is the difference between NDT consulting and NDT inspection services?
faq.a: Consulting covers the programme: written practices, procedures, examinations and audit support under a Level III. Inspection is the hands-on examination of parts, welds and assets by qualified Level I and Level II technicians. Atlantis NDT provides both, scoped and quoted separately.

level3.h1: ASNT Level III Consulting — Your Outside NDT Level 3 Consultant for Written Practices, Procedures and Audits
level3.intro: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT Level III consulting as an outside agency: NDT Level 3 consulting services for companies that need Level III authority without a Level III on the payroll. Your company stays the certifying employer. The Level III writes and approves the technical documents, prepares and grades examinations, and supports your audits.

qa.h2: What is an outsourced NDT Level III?
qa.answer: An outsourced NDT Level III is an ASNT Level III engaged from outside your company, an outside agency Level III, who carries out the Level III duties your written practice assigns: approving procedures and techniques, preparing and grading examinations, and overseeing personnel qualification. Your company remains the certifying employer.
more: Either way the arrangement is written into the employer's written practice, which names what the outside Level III signs.

What stays with your company: the written practice itself, the decision to certify, the certificates and the records. What the outside agency Level III brings: the technical approval, the examinations and the audit-ready paperwork behind each certification.
qa.founder: Atlantis's Level III work is led by founder Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in five methods (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), with 11+ years of international NDT field experience. A Level III approves only within the methods they hold, so every proposal names the methods it covers.

covers.h2: What our NDT Level III consulting covers
covers.p: Written practices to ASNT SNT-TC-1A and ANSI/ASNT CP-189; NDT procedures and technique sheets approved within the Level III's certified methods; personnel qualification, examinations and vision-test records; and audit preparation and responses for customer, supplier and ISO-style audits. Aerospace programmes under the customer-specified aerospace standard are covered by our ASNT NDT Level III consulting, described further down this page.

deliverables.h2: What a Level III engagement delivers

items.name: Written practice
items.text: A written practice to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189, issued as a controlled document with approval signatures and revision history.

items.name: Procedures and technique sheets
items.text: NDT procedures and technique sheets written or reviewed, then approved within the Level III's methods.

items.text: General, specific and practical examinations prepared, administered and graded, with the records your certification files need.

items.text: The Level III functions your written practice assigns, on a retainer or per engagement, while your company stays the certifying employer.

process.h2: How a Level III engagement runs

steps.p: Agree the methods, levels, codes and customer specifications in scope, and who signs certifications for your company.
Read your written practice, procedures and technician files against SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 and your customer requirements.
Issue drafts with every open question marked, then approve the final written practice, procedures and technique sheets.
Prepare and grade the examinations; your company then certifies its people against the approved written practice.
Remain your outside agency Level III for audits, procedure revisions and recertification, if you want that cover.

process.note: Each proposal sets its own timeline, because it rests on the scope and on how quickly records are available.

choose.h2: How to choose an outside Level III
choose.intro: Five questions settle most of the decision:
items: Which methods do you hold ASNT NDT Level III in, and can I check them? A Level III approves only within those methods.
Have you written practices and procedures for our codes and customer specifications, such as ASME Section V, AWS D1.1 or a client's own standard?
What do you sign, and what stays with us? Certification stays with the employer; the outside Level III signs what the written practice assigns.
How will you treat our existing procedures: rewrite them, review them, or approve them as written?

audit.h2: The four signatures an auditor traces
paragraphs: An auditor does not assess your Level III in the abstract. The auditor picks a technician's certificate and walks backwards through four signatures, stopping at the first one that is missing, unsigned, out of method scope or out of date: written practice approval, procedure approval, examination approval and grading, and the qualification recommendation behind the certificate.

SNT-TC-1A anchors the first and the third: the employer's written practice is on file and approved by the employer's Level III, and the Level III approves and grades the examinations given for certification. ASME Section V, Article 1 (T-150) anchors the second where the referencing Code Section requires examinations to a written procedure. The fourth is the one firms get wrong: an outside Level III recommends qualification, and the certifying signature belongs to the employer. [NDT written practice development](/ndt-written-practice-development) covers the document at the top of the chain.

methodScope.h2: Method scope: the limit on every signature
paragraphs: Every one of those signatures is bounded by method. Certification is granted method by method, so a Level III certified in UT and PT approves UT and PT procedures and grades UT and PT examinations, and cannot reach other methods with the same signature. Seniority does not extend scope, and neither does a customer's willingness to accept it at the time.

Two controls keep an arrangement inside its scope. The scope statement lists the methods covered, the scheme each was certified under and the certification expiry; ASNT NDT Level III certification renews on a five-year cycle. And adding a method triggers a scope review before the first procedure in it is written. See [what an outside Level III can and cannot sign](/consulting/outside-ndt-level-3-can-and-cannot-do).

items.q: Can an outside Level III sign our written practice?
items.a: Yes, and it is one of the main reasons firms engage one. SNT-TC-1A requires the written practice to be on file and approved by the employer's Level III, and an outside agency Level III designated in that document satisfies the requirement. An auditor checks two things: that the person holds current certification in the relevant methods, and that the involvement is genuine and documented rather than a name on a cover sheet.

items.q: Can an outside agency certify my NDT employees?
items.a: No. Under SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based, so your company issues and signs the certificates. An outside Level III supplies the approving authority: written practice, examinations, procedure approval and oversight. The certifying employer remains you.

UT (including the phased array and TOFD techniques), RT, MT, PT and VT, the five methods in which the founder holds ASNT NDT Level III certification. Other methods need a Level III certified in them; that is raised at scoping and named in the proposal, never covered by extending a signature beyond its scope.

items.q: Our Level III resigned: what happens to our certifications?
items.a: Existing certifications remain valid, but the authority that approved them has gone. Until a replacement Level III is designated, no new personnel can be qualified, no procedure can be approved, and the next audit will ask who currently holds that authority. Designating an interim outside Level III closes the gap; see [what to do when your Level III resigns](/consulting/ndt-level-3-resigned-what-to-do).

items.q: Is an outside Level III cheaper than hiring one?
items.a: Usually, when your Level III work is intermittent: a staff Level III is a full salary against demand that comes in cycles of written practice reviews, procedure approvals, examinations and audits. The comparison turns on how often you qualify people and approve procedures rather than on headcount alone, and the proposal is quoted on that scope.

items.q: Which scheme applies: SNT-TC-1A or CP-189?
items.a: Your customer contract decides. Contracts specifying ANSI/ASNT CP-189 impose a standard using "shall" rather than a recommended practice. Absent either, SNT-TC-1A employer-based certification is the default across US industrial work.

items.q: Does an outside Level III cover a Nadcap audit?
items.a: A designated Responsible Level 3 satisfies the personnel-authority requirement under the customer-specified aerospace standard, which AC7114 assesses. It does not by itself close the record findings that generate most Nadcap results: vision test currency, OJT documentation and retained examination papers remain the employer's responsibility.

items.q: Can a fractional Level III sign off on new inspection procedures?
items.a: Yes. Procedure and technique approval is core to the Level III role whether the engagement is full-time or outsourced; what changes with a fractional arrangement is the review cadence, not the signature authority. The approval stays within the methods the Level III holds.

items.q: What does an NDT Level III consultant do?
items.a: An NDT Level III consultant writes and approves the documents your NDT programme runs on (the written practice, procedures and technique sheets), administers and grades the qualification examinations, interprets codes and standards, and supports audits. The consultant acts for your company; your company remains the employer that certifies its technicians.

items.q: Will our customers accept a procedure approved by an outsourced Level III?
items.a: Generally yes, when the outside Level III is named in your written practice, holds the method certification and the approval is documented. Some aerospace primes and operators require their own approval of outside Level IIIs, so check each customer's requirements before relying on it.
